subject: VAL
label: Grade 03
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 03 Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Learning from mistakes
modules.outcome: describe a mistake and what was learned
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Learning from mistakes', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe a mistake and what was learned. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Learning from mistakes' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: describe a mistake and what was learned. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: Empathy steps: notice, ask, listen, say back what you heard, offer help. After a mistake: what happened, what I learned, what I will do next. Method: Model run for 'Learning from mistakes'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe a mistake and what was learned: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.

modules.outcome: plan a small act of service
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Kindness in action', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: plan a small act of service. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Kindness in action' and say what it means in your own words.

Use it: plan a small act of service. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: A classmate drops books. Kind action: help pick them up and say 'Are you OK?'. Reflect: how did it feel for them, and for you? Method: Model run for 'Kindness in action'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Plan a small act of service: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Pick a need: Hessa's class notices the school cleaner works hard, and the plant pots at the school door are dry. Hessa asks, 'What small act of service could we do for our school this week?'

Step 2, Choose one act: The class lists three ideas: write thank-you cards to the cleaner, water the plants, or pick up litter on the field. They vote by raising hands: 12 for cards, 8 for plants, 6 for litter. Cards win.

Step 3, Plan the act: Hessa writes the plan. Who: all 26 children. What: one thank-you card each. When: Tuesday morning. Materials: paper and crayons. Check: 12 plus 8 plus 6 is 26 votes, so every child voted once.

Step 4, Split jobs: Each child writes 'Thank you for keeping our school clean' plus their name and a drawing. Hessa gives out paper, Ali collects the cards in a box, and the teacher helps tie them with a ribbon.
Step 5, Do it: On Tuesday the class gives the box of 26 cards to the cleaner. She smiles and says, 'This makes my day.' Nobody asked for a reward, because the act was given freely and kindly.
Step 6, Reflect: Hessa says, 'We helped one person feel noticed. It cost no money and took ten minutes.' Next week the class plans the plant watering. A small planned act can happen again and again.

Your turn: Plan a small act of service for a neighbour or the school library. Model answer: act is tidying library books on Wednesday; who is four children, jobs are sort, stack, label; check that all books return to the right shelf.

modules.title: Teamwork
modules.outcome: work in a group and share jobs fairly
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Teamwork', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: work in a group and share jobs fairly. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Teamwork' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: work in a group and share jobs fairly. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: A friend says 'skip class'. Steps: stay calm, say no clearly, offer another plan, walk away, tell a trusted adult if it continues. Method: Model run for 'Teamwork'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Work in a group and share jobs fairly: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, The task: Group of four, Omar, Dina, Hamad and Sana, must build a poster about water saving in 30 minutes. The poster has four parts: title, a picture, three tips and colouring.

Step 2, Share jobs fairly: They list the jobs and match strengths. Omar writes the title, Dina draws the picture, Hamad writes the three tips, and Sana does the colouring. Four jobs, four children, one job each.
Step 3, Check time: The group plans time. Title 5 minutes, picture 10, tips 10, colouring 5. Total is 5 plus 10 plus 10 plus 5, which is 30 minutes. The plan fits exactly the time they have.

Step 4, A problem: Hamad finishes his tips in 6 minutes, not 10. Dina has not finished drawing. Hamad says, 'I am done, can I help?' Dina says yes and he draws the water drops, so the picture finishes on time.

Step 5, Listening: When Sana wants a blue border and Omar prefers green, they listen to each other and vote with Dina and Hamad. Three of four choose blue. Omar accepts the result politely and helps colour.

Step 6, Result and reflection: The poster is done in 28 minutes, with the whole group's names on it. They say, 'We shared jobs, helped each other and listened.' Teamwork meant nobody did everything and nobody did nothing.

Your turn: A team of three must make a model of a bridge from boxes in 20 minutes. Assign jobs and time. Model answer: Child A cuts boxes 8 minutes, B glues 8 minutes, C paints 4 minutes; 8+8+4=20; whoever finishes early helps another.
